subject: Renewal: Omnicorp Dedicated Expansion and Q3-Q4 Capacity Plan
messages:
From: Emily Zhou <e.zhou@omnicorp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Victor Ramos <v.ramos@omnicorp.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning and capacity needs for Q3/Q4

Hi Tessa,

We are starting our procurement cycle for the Oct 1 renewal. Traffic has accelerated faster than we modeled earlier and leadership wants a clear recommendation for committed GPUs and throughput guarantees. High level context:
- Current Dedicated pool: 32 GPUs, mixed A100/RTX; peak sustained QPS = 75, p95 latency target 200ms.
- Last quarter saw an average token growth of +28% month-over-month for the text-generation endpoint.

Request: could you share a capacity plan for Oct 1 renewal that covers conservative and upside scenarios through Dec 31, including recommended GPU counts, reserved pool sizing, and any suggested SLAs or burst policies? Attach our raw telemetry if helpful.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhou
VP Product, Omnicorp
emily.zhou@omnicorp.com

-----
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhou <e.zhou@omnicorp.com>
Cc: Victor Ramos <v.ramos@omnicorp.com>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal planning and capacity needs for Q3/Q4

Emily,

Thanks for the heads up and the telemetry you attached. I ran a conservative forecast and an upside scenario and attached the modeling workbook we used. Summary below.

Quick TLDR
- Conservative (base case): expect peak sustained QPS to grow from 75 to 110 by Oct 1, token/sec growth ~3.5x since March. Recommend moving to a 48-GPU reserved pool (additional 16 GPUs) with a 10% burst buffer.
- Upside (high growth): if monthly token growth stays >20%, peak QPS could reach 160 by Dec 31. Recommend a staged bump: 48 GPUs at renewal with an option to add +8 GPUs on a 30-day notice (commit discount for the first 60 days).
- Model notes: these numbers assume continued use of the same model family and average prompt lengths. If you move to a longer-context model or larger base model, we'll need to re-run kernel selection and may recommend more GPUs.

Key metrics (Oct 1 snapshot)
- Base QPS target: 110
- p95 latency target: 200ms end-to-end
- Token throughput: ~950k tokens/sec across the pool at base case
- Recommended GPUs: 48 total reserved (32 current -> +16), 10% burst capacity via shared burst credits

Operational asks
- Confirm whether traffic is evenly distributed across regions or concentrates in us-east. If multi-region, we may recommend a small regional mirror for failover.
- Confirm any hard latency guarantees beyond p95 200ms.

Attached: omnicorp_growth_input.csv with your telemetry, and a workbook with scenario modeling.

Next steps: Connor will follow up with a draft amendment and the proposed reserved pool pricing and commitment options. Happy to jump on a call with your infra leads.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0147

From: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhou <e.zhou@omnicorp.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed reserved pool and pricing — Omnicorp renewal

Emily, team —

Following Tessa's forecast, here is our recommended commercial configuration and the operational guarantees we can include in the Oct 1 amendment. Full config attached as proposed_pool_config.pdf.

Commercial proposal (summary)
- Base reserved pool: 48 GPUs dedicated to Omnicorp (adds 16 GPUs to current commit).
- Burst buffer: 10% of pool (allowing short bursts up to 52 GPUs for up to 120s per 10-minute window).
- Upside option: right to add 8 GPUs with 30 days notice at a 10% uplift on unit price for the first 60 days; greater discounts for 12-month commitment.
- Pricing: blended monthly reservation fee with usage overage at 70% of on-demand token unit price. Exact numbers in the attached PDF and HubSpot deal.

Performance & capacity rationale
- Base case GPU estimate: 48 GPUs supports ~1.0M tokens/sec (aggregate) for your current model mix with target p95 200ms. That maps to the 110 QPS base case when accounting for average tokens per response.
- Upside plan capacity: adding +8 GPUs raises aggregate token throughput by ~16% which covers spikes up to ~160 QPS with sustained short bursts.
- Reliability: propose a two-zone placement for half the pool to protect against AZ-level capacity events. This keeps effective availability >99.95% under our SLA model.

SLA & guarantees
- SLA target: 99.9% availability for the reserved pool, with credits tied to downtime windows.
- Latency guardrail: p95 200ms target; if we miss p95 for two consecutive weeks, automatic canary scale to burst buffer and rollback to older model variant if needed.

Operational items for the amendment
- Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones for procurement sign-off, SOC 2 evidence exchange, and network setup.
- Legal: short amendment to add GPUs, update pricing, and define burst rules.
- Technical review scheduled Aug 4 to validate telemetry and placement.

Please let me know if you want the initial amendment drafted with the upside option built into the pricing schedule. If you approve, I'll ask legal to prepare the redline and send a DocuSign link.

Cheers,
Connor Obrien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_pool_config.pdf (summary of SKU, pricing tiers, and placement recommendations)

Subject: RE: Proposed reserved pool and pricing — Omnicorp renewal

Thanks, Connor and Tessa — this looks reasonable and in line with what leadership expects. Two quick asks before we sign:
1) Can you add a clause that the 30-day add-on for +8 GPUs can be exercised twice during the 12-month term?
2) Can you confirm the regional placement will keep at least 40% capacity in us-east where most traffic originates?

If those are fine, we will proceed with the amendment and legal prep. Please send the DocuSign when ready and include the MAP milestones (procurement complete, network whitelist, SOC 2 evidence).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Emily
VP Product, Omnicorp
